lessons.title: What is Money?
lessons.description: Learn the basics of money and why we use it

content.text: Money is something we use to buy things we need and want. But where does it come from?

content.title: Fun Fact!
content.text: A long time ago, people traded things like shells, beads, and even salt as money!

content.title: Why Do We Use Money?
points: To buy food, clothes, and toys
To save for things we want later
To pay people for their work

content.title: Real Life Example
content.text: When you do chores, your parents might give you an allowance. That's your money for helping out!

quiz.question: What is money used for?
options: To buy things we need and want
quiz.explanation: Money helps us buy all kinds of things - food, clothes, toys, and more!

quiz.question: What did people use as money long ago?
quiz.explanation: Before paper money, people traded items like shells, beads, and even salt!

quiz.question: Why do parents give allowance?
quiz.explanation: Allowance is money you earn by doing chores and helping around the house!

lessons.title: Saving vs. Spending
lessons.description: Learn when to save and when to spend your money

content.text: You have money - now what? Should you spend it all or save some? Let's find out!

content.title: What is Saving?
points: Building up money for something big

content.title: What is Spending?
points: Using money to buy things now
Trading money for items or experiences
Making choices about what to buy

content.title: The 50-30-20 Rule for Kids
content.text: Try dividing your money: 50% for spending, 30% for saving, 20% for sharing!

content.title: Real Life Example
content.text: You get $10. You could spend it all on candy, or save $5 for a toy you really want next month!

quiz.question: What does saving mean?
quiz.explanation: Saving means keeping your money safe so you can use it later for something special!

quiz.question: If you get $10, what's a smart way to use it?
options: Spend it all on candy right away
Hide it and forget about it
quiz.explanation: It's smart to save some money while also enjoying some now. Balance is key!

quiz.question: Why is saving important?
quiz.explanation: Saving helps you buy bigger, better things you really want in the future!

lessons.title: Setting Goals
lessons.description: Learn how to set and achieve your money goals

content.text: A goal is something you want to achieve. Money goals help you get things you really want!

content.title: Types of Goals
points: Short-term: Things you want soon (like a new toy)
Medium-term: Things that take longer (like a video game)
Long-term: Big things (like a bike or tablet)

content.title: How to Set a Goal
content.text:
1. Pick something you want
2. Find out how much it costs
3. Figure out how much to save each week
4. Track your progress!

content.title: Real Life Example
content.text: You want a $30 toy. If you save $3 each week, you'll have enough in 10 weeks!

content.title: Fun Fact!
content.text: When you reach a goal, your brain releases happy chemicals! Setting goals feels great!

quiz.question: What is a money goal?
quiz.explanation: A money goal is something you're saving up to buy or achieve!

quiz.question: You want a $20 game. If you save $2 per week, how long until you can buy it?
Which is a short-term goal?
options: Getting a candy bar next week
quiz.explanation: A short-term goal is something you can achieve soon, like buying a candy bar!
